Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.
rationale:
The subject's own obligations are that matches are grouped per `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`, excerpts are rendered per `requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`, each entry's `node` is a reference per `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, and `complete` reports whether the scope was exhausted. The tests cover each of these.

- **Grouping and excerpts:** `project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration]` has one item with a non-ASCII hit (`const[A]`, `éhit`). It has another item with two hits (`const[B]`, `hit hit`). Both pages and results are asserted exactly. `const[B]` produces one entry. Its excerpt is the whole item, so the default window is clipped to the item and the nearby hits are merged into one contiguous excerpt. Each hit's byte span is also asserted.
- **Node reference:** the same test asserts that each entry's `node` equals the interned ID of the enclosing item. It also reads the returned entry through `read_node` and selects the tag through `finish_search`. The tool schema in `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` is checked as well. The later page's `node` is compared with the interned ID of the item that `source_node` maps to.
- **`complete`:** `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` asserts `complete == true` for an unrestricted search. It asserts `complete == false` for `limit: 1` on a source with many hits. `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` asserts `complete == true`. `source_reads_track_optional_dependencies_and_empty_searches_remain_discovery` asserts `{"complete":true,"matches":[]}` for an empty search. `scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness` and `gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository` check `complete` at the SDK level, for both the capped and uncapped cases.

The remaining marked tests (`source_tools_*`, `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads`) check argument forwarding and that discovery registers no reads.

Window detail (`window_bytes` 0, 1 and 2, the 128-byte default, and UTF-8 boundary clipping) has its own dedicated tests in `project_sources.rs`. Examples are `default_windows_retain_128_bytes_on_each_side`, `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries` and `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration`. That detail belongs to `requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`, which this subject only cites, so I did not reassess it here. I found no unaddressed obligation or counterexample.

text: The harness groups matching occurrences under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` and renders each excerpt under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`. Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.

Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.

The harness represents a `NodeId<D>` as an unsigned integer. Each built-in tool that accepts a node accepts the same top-level address fields, alongside its own arguments (such as an edge `label`). `NodeAddress` in tool signatures denotes these alternatives:
| `node` | Look up the assigned ID in the domain's cache. |

| `path`, optional `location` | Resolve the project-relative file within the domain's visible sources. `location` is its outline selector and defaults to the empty selector for the file root. Resolve the item, map its `OutlineData` through `Domain::source_node`, and intern the resulting identity. |
| `data` | Deserialize the JSON value as `D::NodeData` and intern it in the domain's cache. |

For domains using the agent harness, the tool schema describes `data` using the domain’s JSON schema for `D::NodeData`. The harness uses the same JSON representation when returning and accepting an identity.

Resolving an address is discovery. The requested operation determines which observations enter evidence. Invalid addresses, unavailable files, and unknown selectors produce tool errors before the requested operation runs.
